newsitem.title: UK: Rolls says not hit by budget move on ACT.
newsitem.headline: Rolls says not hit by budget move on ACT.

text.p: Britain's Rolls-Royce Plc said on Wednesday it was not affected by UK's Labour government's decision to scrap tax credits paid to pension funds and companies.
At present, companies pay 20 percent Advance Corporation Tax on dividends, which can be claimed back by tax-exempt investors such as pension funds.
The engineering conglomerate said the changes would not result in its minimum funding requirement (MFR) level for its principal pension schemes falling below 100 percent.
"It will not therefore give rise to an immediate cash injection to meet the MFR funding level, as has been suggested in some press speculation," Rolls-Royce said in a statement.

While announcing the abolition of the tax credits in his budget, UK Chancellor Gordon Brown said: "the present tax system of tax credits encourages companies to pay out dividends rather than invest their profits".
Rolls-Royce's share price remained firm, just 1/2 pence ahead at 235-1/2, at close of trade on Wednesday.
